questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country with beautiful nature, good courses, many university clubs and with good reviews regarding both the Erasmus+ program and housing. University of Limerick in Ireland had it all, so it became my first priority. I'm extremely happy that I got to go to this destination and I can't recommend it enough. :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find information and UL was really good at informing their incoming students in general.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of assistance. We received a weekly email leading up to our start and we would get replies to our emails within hours almost. There was a lot of events in our first week at campus (and throughout our stay) and we could always ask for help if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were multiple villages available with different apartment constellations. I lived in Thomond Village in a 6-person apartment with my own bedroom and ensuite bathroom. However, I know that multiple people did not secure on-campus housing. On-campus accommodation is assigned randomly, and I know that the unlucky students struggled to find housing. Ireland is currently experiencing a bad housing crisis, making the process very frustrating at the moment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchens were fully equipped. There was no meal plans.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Everything works well with laundry facilities, a reception, well-working kitchens and included gym membership.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have given UL accommodation a rating of 5, but I find it problematic that students who aren't selected for accommodation are left on their own almost completely.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There was designated sites for modules and courses which can be found here:
https://bookofmodules.ul.ie
– all this made the progress very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you had questions regarding courses you could always send an email and expect a reply shortly after. The professors I asked for previous syllabus were also quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful and got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask questions and send emails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were fairly easy, while others were perfectly challenging. I felt like I learned quite a lot during my exchange.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was almost no group work, and assignments were individual. UL also used PowerPoint presentations, and their lectures were fairly similar to KU. It was less theoretical, which was a nice change from KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Policy-making in the European Union (replaced EP)
- Comparative European Politics (replaced DAK3)
- Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict (elective)
- Russian Politics (elective)
- Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture (elective)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of my three electives. I really learned a lot in Russian Politics and I really enjoyed Sociology of Gender and Popular Culture. Nationalism, Ethnicity and Conflict was also great, which taught me more about the Irish history too.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter anything unexpected. Personal spending differes quite a lot depended on how many trips we did. I only had to buy one book online, the rest was already provided.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The cost of food is about the same as in Denmark if not cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot available for students at UL through the UL Wolves clubs and societies:
https://ulwolves.ie/

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Kayak Club. Went on a weekend trip and tried white water with them which was great. I also got to try a house party with them at Halloween. A great way to meet the locals since not many internationals joined this club. The Surf Club was a bit too popular unfortunately so I gave up on that in the end. The same was the case for Outdoor Pursuits. They took too many students in without being able to take them all on hiking trips. I applied almost every week but never got a spot. The Yoga Society was also great.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We went on trips around the country almost every weekend. I really recommend going to the country side and enjoy a stew and a Guinness at the local pubs. You'll almost always find great live music there. I loved Connemara and Killarney National Park. Use All Trails for finding great hikes. You should also check out Belfast, interesting history. There is a lot to do in Ireland and I didn't get to try everything I wanted to.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy both due to the language but also the people. The Irish people are very helpful and friendly. Everything seems to work fine most of the time.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and societies! And go to pubs of course.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything challenging in particular. Their hostels might be less clean with mold being a bit more common than what is good.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I will miss the pub culture a lot and the events around campus. I will really miss the clubs and societies here, which are a lot more student controlled than at KU.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Ask questions (you'll get answers), join clubs and enjoy the beautiful country of Ireland!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I've covered most of it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met there. I will never forget this time because of them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to leave all of this behind. It was the best semester I've had and probably will have.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Remember to say yes! Go on that trip and don't focus too much on school only. I had a big assignment while I was away in Edinburgh and it turned out just fine writing it in a loud hostel :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
